judge_assessment.explanation: The mathematics is exactly as the judge describes: x(x+5)=x^2+5x; (x+3)(x+5)=x^2+8x+15; -9+6x+4x^3-x^2 orders to 4x^3-x^2+6x-9; x^2+7x+12=(x+3)(x+4); 3(2x+5)=6x+15; the sum is 7x+3; (2x-3)(x+4)=2x^2+5x-12; 6x^3-15x^2=3x^2(2x-5); (2x^3-x)(x^2+4)=2x^5+7x^3-4x; (x+2)(x+6)=x^2+8x+12. But the judge's own wording exposes the defect: it says it 'identified coefficients and degrees in all 10 items', and verify.json contains no coefficient or degree check at all. Problem 3 alone prints ten machine-checkable responses - the coefficient and degree of each of four terms, plus the degree and leading coefficient of the whole polynomial - and verify.json id 3 is a single equiv entry on the standard-form ordering. Problem 1 asks 'how many terms ... and what is the coefficient of x'; id 1 verifies only the expansion. Problem 4 asks for the degree of each factor and of the product; id 4 verifies only the factorisation. Problems 8 and 9 ask for factor lists, degrees and leading coefficients that no entry covers. The judge's second claim, that it 'manually reviewed the equivalent-form explanation', is also singular where the sheet is plural: id 10 is correctly declared manual, but problems 2, 5, 6 and 9 each end in a written explanation and problem 7 says 'Circle the cell that produced the constant term' - a marked representation - with no manual companion anywhere.

strengths_to_preserve: The area model is used as an argument, not an illustration: problem 2 prints a four-cell grid for (x+3)(x+5) and then asks why the answer has three terms, so 'cells count multiplications, terms count what is left after combining like terms' is something the student derives. Problems 1 and 7 extend the same grid to a monomial width and to a negative row (-3), which is where sign errors actually live.

Problem 10 pairs a machine entry (equiv: (x+2)(x+6) = x^2+8x+12) with a correctly declared {'type': 'manual'} entry for the written explanation of how one expression can be both a product of two factors and a sum of three terms. That two-entry pattern is exactly what the rest of the sheet needs and should be the template.

Problem 5 (Jo says it is a sum, Ann says it is a product) makes the terms-versus-factors vocabulary the object of study rather than background, and the key resolves it by naming who describes the expression 'as written' before rewriting it.

root_causes.description: Only the headline transformation of each problem is verified. On a sheet whose declared focus is interpreting terms, factors, coefficients and degree, not one coefficient or degree is bound to a recomputed value - the entries verify expansions, factorisations and orderings instead, so the printed answers for the actual focus are unchecked.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 3 prints a table with Coefficient and Degree columns for four terms plus two follow-up questions; verify.json id 3 is one equiv entry.
worksheet.pdf problem 9 asks for the standard form, the degree, the leading coefficient and a prediction argument; verify.json id 9 is one expand entry (2*x**5 + 7*x**3 - 4*x).
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers lists exactly one value per problem (e.g. '9. 2x^5 + 7x^3 - 4x') although the key body correctly answers all the sub-questions.

root_causes.description: Manual declaration was applied to one problem when five carry open or marked responses, so the build reports the sheet as almost entirely machine-verified while several graded responses are written prose or a circled cell.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 2 ('Explain why in one sentence'), 5 ('name the factors and the terms of each form'), 6 ('explain what happened to the degree') and 9 ('explain how you could have predicted the degree') have no manual entry.
worksheet.pdf problem 7 'Circle the cell that produced the constant term' is a marked representation recorded as a plain expand entry.
verify.json contains exactly one {'type': 'manual'} entry, on id 10.

improvements.title: Verify the coefficients and degrees this sheet is actually about
improvements.proposed_change: Declare one verify entry per requested response and fail the build when a problem's declared slot count exceeds its entries. For this case add eval entries for: id 1 term count 2 and coefficient of x = 5; id 3 the eight table cells (-9 -> coefficient -9, degree 0; 6x -> 6, 1; 4x^3 -> 4, 3; -x^2 -> -1, 2) plus polynomial degree 3 and leading coefficient 4; id 4 factor degrees 1, 1 and product degree 2; id 6 degree 1; id 7 coefficient of x = 5; id 8 the factor list and each factor's degree; id 9 degree 5 and leading coefficient 2.
improvements.regression_test: Add a gate case to tests/ that loads a fixture worksheet whose problem prints N distinct requested responses and a verify JSON covering fewer of them, and assert the build fails with a slot-coverage error. It fails today (no such check exists, so the fixture builds green) and passes once the answer-slot declaration is enforced.
improvements.expected_impact: The sheet's declared focus becomes verified rather than assumed; this is the largest systemic cluster in the run (61 cases) and this case is one of its clearest instances.
improvements.risk: Slot counts declared by hand can be gamed. Derive them from the rendered answer lines and enumerated parts instead of trusting a typed number.

improvements.title: Add manual companions for the explanations in 2, 5, 6, 9 and the circled cell in 7
improvements.proposed_change: Extend the id-10 pattern - a machine entry plus a manual companion on the same id - to problems 2, 5, 6, 7 and 9, and add a build lint over worksheet.tex problem bodies for 'explain', 'circle', 'name the', 'describe' that fails when the id has no manual entry.
improvements.regression_test: Add a gate case to tests/ with a fixture problem whose statement contains an open-response verb ("explain", "name the error", "describe", "circle") and whose verify JSON has no matching manual entry, and assert the build reports an unflagged open response. It fails today (the fixture builds green with exit 0) and passes after the lint lands.
improvements.expected_impact: The manual-review count reported to the teacher rises from 1 to 6 and matches what the sheet actually asks a human to read.
improvements.risk: A verb-based lint over-fires on hints. Scope it to imperatives attached to an answer slot and allow an explicit suppression.

case_summary: Conceptually the richest sheet in my slice and mathematically flawless - I re-expanded, re-combined and re-factored all ten items and every printed value in the key is right. The area model does real work (problem 2 makes 'four cells, three terms' the question), problem 5 turns the terms-versus-factors vocabulary into an argument between two students, and problem 10 already pairs a machine entry with a properly declared manual one. The defect is that verification covers only the headline transformation of each problem: on a sheet titled 'terms, factors, coefficients, and degree', not a single coefficient or degree is machine-checked. Problem 3's table alone prints ten checkable responses against one verify entry. Four more problems end in written explanations and problem 7 asks for a circled cell, none flagged manual. The answer key answers all of it correctly, so nothing a student reads is wrong - the binding between the printed answers and recomputed values is what is missing.
